### Bruiser — Identity, Violence & Belonging

Bruiser (2022) follows Darious, a teenager struggling with his identity, family relationships, and place in the world. Living with a strict father who pushes him to become tougher, Darious finds himself caught between the expectations placed on him and the person he wants to become.

His life takes an unexpected turn when he meets Porter, a mysterious older man who offers him a different perspective on strength, masculinity, and freedom. As their connection grows, Darious begins questioning everything he has been taught about being a man and how he should handle conflict.

However, Porter's influence brings new complications, forcing Darious to confront painful truths about his family and himself. As tensions rise, he must decide what kind of person he wants to become and whether real strength comes from violence or understanding.

The film explores themes of identity, fatherhood, masculinity, anger, and belonging. It shows how the desire to be accepted can lead someone toward dangerous choices, especially when they are searching for guidance in the wrong places.

What makes Bruiser compelling is its emotional portrayal of a young man trying to understand himself while navigating the difficult relationships that shape his future.

💬 Sometimes the hardest fight isn't against someone else—it's figuring out who you want to become.
